source_caption:
Tulsa King — Power, Loyalty & Starting Over

Tulsa King (2022) follows Dwight “The General” Manfredi, a New York Mafia capo who is released from prison after spending 25 years behind bars. Expecting to return to his old life, Dwight quickly discovers that the organization he once served has no place for him anymore.

Instead, he is sent to Tulsa, Oklahoma, where he knows almost no one and has no established influence. Rather than accept being pushed aside, Dwight begins building his own criminal operation from scratch, using his experience, confidence, and old-school Mafia mentality to establish control.

As Dwight recruits new allies and expands his business, he attracts attention from local criminals and law enforcement. At the same time, his relationship with the New York Mafia becomes increasingly complicated, forcing him to deal with enemies both near and far.

The series explores themes of loyalty, ambition, reinvention, family, and power. It shows how a man can lose everything he once built and still find a way to create something new—but rebuilding an empire comes with enemies determined to tear it down.

What makes Tulsa King compelling is watching an old-school gangster enter a completely unfamiliar world and turn a fresh start into a new criminal empire.

💬 After 25 years in prison, Dwight didn't come home—he built a new kingdom.

source_details.synopsis: Tulsa King is an American comedy and crime drama television series created by Taylor Sheridan for the streaming platform Paramount+. The series stars Sylvester Stallone as Dwight "The General" Manfredi, an American Mafia caporegime who has been recently released from prison in New York and is sent to Tulsa, Oklahoma, where he begins to set up a criminal organization. It is Stallone's first leading role in a scripted television series. The series also stars Andrea Savage, Martin Starr, Jay Will, Max Casella, Domenick Lombardozzi, Vincent Piazza, A. C.
